items.title: If Day 3's bug had slipped through, how many users would it have actually hit?
items.description: L2 and L3's scenario catches a checkout bug at a 5% rollout. Drag the rollout percentage and your total user base to see how many real people a bug would reach at that stage — this is the concrete reason gradual widening (5% -> 25% -> 100%) bounds risk instead of just delaying it.

params.name: rolloutPercent
params.label: Rollout percentage when the bug is caught

items.compute:
const usersExposed = Math.round((params.rolloutPercent / 100) * params.totalUsers);
return { usersExposed };

outputs.label: Users exposed to the bug before it's caught

items.title: How fast does 'a few flags' turn into 'untestable'?
items.description: Matching L3's countPathCombinations(n) = 2^n: each simultaneously active flag doubles the code paths a change could interact with. Drag the number of active flags to see how quickly manual verification becomes impossible — this is the concrete cost the flag lifecycle's cleanup stage exists to prevent.
items.compute:
const pathCombinations = Math.pow(2, params.activeFlags);
return { pathCombinations };
